evals.prompt: I just finished the order list endpoint on this branch — test the backend change.
evals.expected_output: A test plan covering pagination boundaries, sort-field exposure, tenant isolation and the status filter, not just happy path + auth + validation.
assertions: Plan includes a case proving tenant isolation: a second tenant lists orders and does not see the first tenant's rows
Plan includes a case requesting a page beyond the last page and expects an empty page rather than an error
Plan includes a case sending size above the configured max (100) and expects the size to be capped
Plan includes a case sending size=0 or a non-positive size
Plan includes a case sorting on a field that is not part of the response DTO (sort-parameter property-path exposure)
Plan includes a case for the status filter with an unknown or invalid status value
Plan includes an authentication-failure case (no or invalid token expects 401)
Plan includes a case verifying the new V7 index or that the list query is tenant-scoped at the SQL level
Plan includes a case asserting the documented default sort (createdAt, newest first) is what the endpoint actually returns
Plan includes a case exercising an untouched neighbour endpoint (GET /api/orders/{id}) as a regression check
Plan contains at least 8 distinct numbered test cases
Every case that exercises an endpoint includes a concrete runnable curl command (DB-only, migration, mail or index checks are exempt)
Plan contains a scenario coverage table that marks non-applicable categories N/A with a stated reason

evals.prompt: capture endpoint is done, verify the API works
evals.expected_output: A test plan covering idempotent replay, concurrent double-capture, invalid state transitions, amount boundaries, role and ownership checks, and the published event.
assertions: Plan includes an idempotency replay case: the same Idempotency-Key sent twice returns the same body and captures only once
Plan includes a concurrency case firing overlapping capture requests and proving only one capture landed in the DB
Plan includes an invalid state transition case (capturing a payment that is already CAPTURED, VOIDED, PENDING or EXPIRED)
Plan includes a case capturing more than the authorized amount and expecting rejection
Plan includes amount boundary cases (0, negative, and more than two decimal places)
Plan includes a partial-capture happy path where amount is less than the authorized amount
Plan includes an authorization case for a caller without the MERCHANT role expecting 403
Plan includes an ownership case where another merchant's payment id returns 404 rather than 403
Plan includes a case for an unknown payment id returning 404
Plan verifies the payments.captured event was actually published, checked outside the HTTP response (queue, outbox or broker API)
At least one negative case verifies the DB after the call to prove no state change occurred
Plan includes a case verifying the V12 migration artefacts (captured_amount column and idempotency_key table)
Plan contains at least 10 distinct numbered test cases
Every case that exercises an endpoint includes a concrete runnable curl command (DB-only, migration, mail or index checks are exempt)
Plan contains a scenario coverage table that marks non-applicable categories N/A with a stated reason

evals.prompt: small fix, emails should be case insensitive now. test it
evals.expected_output: A test plan that treats a three-file bug fix seriously: case and whitespace duplicates, the migration reaching existing rows, the mail side effect, the missing ownership check, and the self-conflict edge case.
assertions: Plan includes a case where a differently-cased version of an existing address is rejected as a duplicate
Plan includes a case where an address with leading or trailing whitespace is rejected as a duplicate
Plan verifies with a DB query that the stored address is lower-cased and trimmed
Plan includes a case checking the V21 back-fill reached rows that existed before the change, not only newly created ones
Plan flags or tests the risk that the new unique index fails if two existing rows collide once lower-cased
Plan verifies the verification e-mail side effect outside the HTTP response (mailpit or the mail API)
Plan includes a negative case proving no verification e-mail is sent when the change is rejected
Plan verifies emailVerified is reset to false in the database after a successful change
Plan includes an authorization case: one user attempting to change another user's e-mail
Plan includes the no-op case of patching a user to their own current address (which the new existsByEmailIgnoreCase check can wrongly reject as a self-conflict)
Plan includes a case for an unknown user id returning 404
Plan contains at least 6 distinct numbered test cases
Every case that exercises an endpoint includes a concrete runnable curl command (DB-only, migration, mail or index checks are exempt)
Plan contains a scenario coverage table that marks non-applicable categories N/A with a stated reason
